To run a per-ticket worktree stack\nalongside an already-running one, offset the _hundreds_ digit and take a contiguous\npair — first pair where **both** ports are free:\n\n| Stack        | web  | api  |\n| ------------ | ---- | ---- |\n| default      | 3000 | 3001 |\n| 2nd worktree | 3100 | 3101 |\n| 3rd worktree | 3200 | 3201 |\n\n```bash\nfor base in 3100 3200 3300 3400; do\n  lsof -nP -iTCP:$base       -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1 && continue\n  lsof -nP -iTCP:$((base+1)) -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1 && continue\n  echo \"web=$base api=$((base+1))\"; break\ndone\n```\n\n`+100` rather than `+10` clears the whole reserved 3000–3003 block in one step, and\nkeeps each stack's pair visually adjacent.\n\n**Move web AND api together — never the web alone.** The API's `CORS_ORIGIN` is a\nsingle origin, so a web on a new port pointed at the _shared_ default API is blocked by\nthe browser and **no login POST fires**. A second stack with its own API and a matching\n`CORS_ORIGIN` is the supported shape, and it works: measured on web 3100 → api 3101, the\npreflight returns `204` with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:3100`.\n\n**Everything below the app tier is a singleton and is NOT offset** — Postgres 5432,\nFloci (S3) 9000, LocalStack 4566, Cognito emulator 9229, Lambda 9221, adminer 8080. Two\nstacks therefore **share one `cdsdb`**: running one branch's migrations mutates the other\nworktree's data. Before starting a second stack, confirm nothing is pending\n(`SELECT count(*) FROM migrations` vs `ls cds-api/src/db/migrations/*.ts | wc -l`) and\ndo **not** run migrations from two diverging branches against the same DB.\n\n**Never `docker compose up` from a second worktree.** Compose derives the project name\nfrom the directory, so it starts a _second_ project that collides on 5432/9000. Join the\nrunning one explicitly, naming the project:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -p cds-app-rewrite --profile dev up -d localstack\n```\n\nA fresh worktree also needs the **gitignored root `.env`** copied in first, or compose\naborts with `required variable MIGRATION_DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET is missing a value`.\n\n### Targeting an offset stack — use `--base` / `--api` (CDS-2057)\n\n`scripts/cds-session.mjs` resolves base URLs from `scripts/demo-users.json`, where `local`\nis hardcoded to `{\"base\":\"http://localhost:3000\",\"api\":\"http://localhost:3001\"}`. That\nregistry entry is still the default, but it is no longer the only option: `--base` and\n`--api` override it per run, so a second worktree's offset stack is reachable by the\nnormal verification path.\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/cds-session.mjs --env local --as system.admin --base http://localhost:3100 --api http://localhost:3101 --probe /dashboard\n```\n\nThe overrides are applied **before** the resolved-host re-assert, so they are subject to\nexactly the same `ALLOWED_HOST` allowlist as a registry entry — verified: a prod host, a\nprod API host and an arbitrary host are each refused with exit 2, while `localhost:<port>`\nis accepted. Overriding one of the pair is honoured; the API's `CORS_ORIGIN` must still\nname the web origin or no login request fires at all (see the CORS rule above).\n\n**Still do not hand-roll a Playwright login** to reach a stack — that is the\n`fill()`-vs-`type()` trap the harness exists to prevent\n([browser-verification](browser-verification.md)).\n\n_Was previously recorded here as a hard gap (\"no flag or env var retargets it\"); the\noverride closed it. The diagnosis in that note was right — the restriction was the\nregistry, not the guard._\n\n## Migration dashboard database\n\n- `migration-dashboard/data/migration_dashboard.db` is **gitignored** and must\n  **NEVER** be committed. It is a local runtime artifact that changes with every\n  pipeline run.\n\n## Automated hook\n\n`.claude/settings.json` runs `tsc --noEmit` after every Edit/Write. A failing\ntypecheck surfaces immediately — fix it before moving on.\n\n## Running tests / `tsc` in a fresh `git worktree`\n\nA new worktree off `origin/main` has **no `node_modules`**, and this monorepo\n**hoists** `jest`/`ts-jest`/`tsc` to the **repo-root** `node_modules` (not the\nper-package ones). Consequences and the fix:\n\n- **Symlink deps from the primary checkout** (they're branch-independent):\n  ```bash\n  ln -s <primary>/node_modules      <wt>/node_modules\n  ln -s <primary>/cds-api/node_modules  <wt>/cds-api/node_modules\n  ln -s <primary>/cds-web/node_modules  <wt>/cds-web/node_modules\n  ```\n  Do **not** `npx jest` — with no local install it silently installs a fresh\n  jest that can't find `ts-jest` and fails.\n- **Let each package's own config apply.** `cds-api` keeps its jest config in\n  `package.json`; `cds-web` uses `jest.config.js`. Run the root-linked binary\n  (`<wt>/node_modules/.bin/jest <pattern>`) from the package dir and pass **no**\n  `--rootDir`/`--config` — overriding `rootDir` breaks the `^@src/` / `^@/`\n  `moduleNameMapper` and every import fails to resolve.\n- **Before committing:** remove the symlinks (root `node_modules` shows as\n  `?? node_modules`) and **stage files explicitly** — never `git add -A` in a\n  symlinked worktree, or you risk committing the link.\n- Pre-existing `.js` `ts-jest` \"allowJs\" warnings from `packages/shared-constants`\n  are noise — not your error.\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/6-operations/v1-production-is-read-only.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# V1 Production Is Read-Only\n\nOwns the **V1 side** of the migration: the live Windows host that serves V1 for every\njurisdiction. V2's deploy/hotfix discipline is\n[production-hotfix-and-sql](production-hotfix-and-sql.md); this file owns V1 only.\n\n---\n\n## Must-not-miss (stated in full)\n\n### The V1 host must never be modified. There is no staging V1.\n\nOne Windows Server box (`SSH_HOST` in `v1_data_migration_app/.env`) runs the live V1\napp and its MySQL for **all** jurisdictions. Every customer still using V1 is on it.\nThere is no second copy to make a mistake on.\n\nProhibited: writing, creating, deleting, moving or renaming any file; `INSERT` /\n`UPDATE` / `DELETE` / DDL; restarting services, editing config, installing anything.\nThe sole exception is the sanctioned cleanup below, and only under its conditions.\n\nPermitted, and the only things permitted:\n\n- `SELECT` through the SSH tunnel\n- `dir` / SFTP `get` — listing and **reading** files, including to vendor them locally\n\n### A lock is a production side effect. So is anything that changes server state.\n\nThe permitted list above is `SELECT` and `dir`/`get`. It is a list, not a category — do\nnot read it as \"reads are fine.\" `LOCK TABLES ... READ` writes nothing and returns no rows,\nand it is still **not a read**: it changes state other sessions can observe, because a read\nlock blocks every writer to that table until it is released. Anything in that shape —\nlocks, `SET GLOBAL`, `KILL`, a temp table, an advisory lock — has to be **accounted for\nexplicitly** before it runs against V1, not waved through because it returns no rows.\n\nThis is not hypothetical. V1's own report scripts do it, and the vendored copies CDS-2059\nruns still do it against the live production MySQL over the tunnel:\n\n| Script (those actually invoked) | `progs` | `reports` | `comms` | locks per render |\n| ------------------------------- | ------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------- |\n| `svale/csarc.pl`                | 1       | 3         | –       | 4                |\n| `salinca/csarc.pl`              | 1       | 3         | –       | 4                |\n| `smatca/csarc.pl`               | 1       | 2         | –       | 3                |\n| `svale/app2025arc.pl`           | 2       | 3         | –       | 5                |\n| `svale/app2026arc.pl`           | 2       | 3         | –       | 5                |\n| `svale/evqarc.pl`               | 0       | 1         | 0       | 1                |\n| `svale/app2023arc.pl` / `app2024arc.pl` | 0 | 0      | –       | 0                |\n\nUnlock calls match or exceed lock calls in every one of them, and MySQL drops a session's\nlocks on disconnect, so the exposure per report is one short window rather than a leak. The\nreason to care is **volume**: this is a loop over up to ~5,500 reports per jurisdiction with\n`PERL_TIMEOUT_S = 180`, where V1's UI does it once per human page view.\n\n**Two things about this you cannot learn from a run, which is the actual lesson:**\n\n- **Two different MySQL accounts are in play, and only one of them is documented.** Python's\n  worklist query uses the migration app's own account, which `report_pdfs_extractor.py:612`\n  correctly describes as read-only. The perl authenticates separately, as\n  `V1_RENDER_DB_USER` out of `data/header*.scq` — and that is the account issuing the locks.\n  `LOCK TABLES` needs its own privilege on top of `SELECT`, so that account is either not\n  SELECT-only or its locks are silently failing. **Nothing in the repo records its grants**;\n  a full sweep of every `V1_RENDER_DB_USER` reference found credentials plumbing and no\n  statement of privilege anywhere. Do not read the read-only comment as covering it — it is\n  scoped to the worklist by its own wording.\n- If the grant is missing, the failure is **silent**. `perl5/Mysql.pm:185-203` returns `undef`\n  when `prepare`/`execute` fails, and every caller does `$execute = $DB->query($qryrdrp)` and\n  then overwrites `$execute` with the next SELECT. The SELECT still runs, just unlocked, so\n  the render succeeds either way and the output is identical.\n\nSo before running V1 code that locks, establish the account's grants (`SHOW GRANTS`) and say\nwhich of the two worlds you are in. \"It rendered fine\" is not evidence either way.\n\n**Open decision, not a settled prohibition.** These locks are V1's own code, and the reason\nthe scripts are vendored unmodified is that an edited renderer is no longer evidence of what\nV1 produced. So \"just delete the `LOCK TABLES` lines\" trades a small production side effect\nfor a faithfulness problem, and that is a human call, not an implementer's. Until it is\ntaken, the requirement is disclosure: state the lock volume and the grant status in the PR\nrather than letting the comment at `report_pdfs_extractor.py:612` imply the question was\nalready answered.\n\nCount locks by the **`query()` call sites**, not by grepping the statement text. `grep -o\n'LOCK TABLES'` also matches inside `UNLOCK TABLES`, and the statements are assigned to\nvariables once near the top and then called repeatedly — so text counts are wrong in both\ndirections. An earlier pass overstated these numbers roughly two-fold and invented an\nunlock asymmetry that does not exist.\n\n### \"It's a read function\" does not make it read-only — grep it first\n\nThe incident behind this rule was not a write command. It was calling a _print_ function\nto capture its return value. `smatca/app2020arcp.pm:594-599`:\n\n```perl\nfor ($i=2;$i<6;$i++) {\n        if ($w[121+$i] eq \"on\") {$cat=\"$Bin/apppdfs/$i/PS/$w[1]-$nm-$w[0].html\";}\n        open (FILE,\">$cat\");\n        print FILE $res;\n        close (FILE);\n}\n```\n\nThe `open` sits **outside** the `if`, so every iteration writes. And `$cat` is a package\nglobal — there is no `use strict` anywhere in this code — so an iteration where the `if`\nis false writes to whatever `$cat` last held, **including from a previous call**. That is\nhow one call while rendering `smatca` overwrote a file under `svale/`.\n\nSo before invoking any V1 code, **grep it for `open(`, `>`, `>>`, `unlink`, `rename`,\n`system`, and non-`SELECT` SQL** — and grep whatever it `require`s. If a write cannot be\nruled out, do not run it on the host.\n\nGrep the **jurisdiction's own copy**, not a sibling. Only `smatca` has this unconditional\n`open`; `berkca/app2020arcp.pm:920-927` and six other jurisdictions guard it with\n`if ($off ne \"Y\")`. Same filename, different behaviour — the usual\n[no-hardcoded-jurisdictions](../4-data/migration-authoring-and-validation.md) trap.\n\n### Never claim \"nothing was written\" from the wrong directory\n\nThe assurance was given twice and was false both times, because the check listed\n`dmdpdfs/` while the module in question writes to `apppdfs/`. Both directory names exist\nunder most jurisdictions, so \"I looked and it was clean\" meant nothing.\n\nA negative claim about production state requires listing **the directory that module\nactually writes to**, unfiltered. Extension filters lie too: a `dir *.html` sweep reported\n10 files where the tree held 53, and the 43 `.pdf` it hid were the evidence for who\nnormally writes there.\n\n### If you discover you have written to V1: stop and say so\n\nReport it immediately with full paths and timestamps, and wait. Do not clean up silently,\nand do not fold it into a status update as an aside. The user decides whether the artifact\nis removed, left, or restored.\n\n### Removing your own accidental writes — the only sanctioned V1 mutation\n\nRequires **explicit human instruction**, and then every one of these:\n\n1. **Establish authorship, and prefer a structural signal to a timestamp.** Timestamps\n   under-counted here: a first pass matched 6 files by modification date and missed 4 more,\n   because `LastWriteTime` cannot distinguish \"created by me\" from \"overwritten by me\".\n   Windows keeps `CreationTime` separately — compare both, and convert the host clock (it\n   runs Pacific). The signal that actually worked was **file type**: the tree held 49\n   `.pdf` written by V1 between 2023 and 2024 and _no_ `.html` before this work began, so\n   every `.html` was attributable.\n2. **Dry-run**, printing every matched path — and read the whole list. A truncated read\n   makes a delete list look shorter than it is.\n3. **A guard that throws on an unexpected match count**, in the same script as the\n   mutation: `if ($t.Count -ne $expected) { throw ... }`.\n4. **List before and after**, and report both.\n5. **Never widen the match** to \"looks like something I made.\" Anything not attributable\n   with evidence stays — as `svale/dmdpdfs/A1270.html` did, being V1's own file that was\n   overwritten rather than created, where deleting would have destroyed more than it fixed.\n\n### Where this leaves the migration\n\nRunning V1's report code **in the migration container against a vendored copy** is the\nstructural fix. That work is CDS-2059 and is **not on `main` yet** — until it lands there is\nno perl in the dashboard image and no vendored tree, so the only compliant option is not to\nrun V1's code at all.\n\n**Be precise about what the container fixed.** It moved the **filesystem** side effects off\nthe host: the `open(\">\")` incident above cannot recur, because the perl writes into the\ncontainer. It did **not** move the **database** side effects — the vendored scripts still\nread their credentials from `data/header*.scq` and dial out to the live production MySQL\nover the tunnel, so every `SELECT` and every `LOCK TABLES` still lands on production. The\ntwo risks are separable and only one of them was addressed; do not let \"it runs in a\ncontainer now\" stand in for \"it no longer touches production.\"\n\n---\n\n_Qualifies on the **severity** axis of the\n[maintenance policy](../README.md#when-a-pattern-earns-a-rule-project-wide): 12 files\ncreated on a single-instance production host serving live customers, one pre-existing\nV1-generated file overwritten (data corruption), and two false \"nothing was written\"\nassurances. A production-data-integrity class earns a rule on first occurrence._\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/6-operations/production-hotfix-and-sql.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Production Fixes\n\n## Deploy path\n\n- Prod deploys go through the **`production`** branch, not `main` (main = staging).\n- A prod fix = hotfix branch off `origin/production`, PR `--base production`.\n- **Verify in UAT first:** open a `--base uat` PR and validate in UAT before the\n  `--base production` PR. Branches in order: `main` / `qa` / `uat` / `production`.\n- **One prod PR bundles ALL of a ticket's code fixes** (not per-issue). UI-only\n  fixes stay out.\n- **Every prod fix must also land on `main`** — a prod hotfix isn't done until an\n  equivalent `main` branch/PR is open, else the next main→prod promotion\n  regresses it.\n\n## One-off prod data SQL\n\n- Track by issue number:\n  `cds-api/src/db/manual-cleanups/CDS-<issue>-<verb>-<desc>.sql` (see dir README).\n- Prefer **admin UI housekeeping over one-off SQL** — SQL is the fallback\n  (blocked-and-can't-wait), not the default.\n- Mutations must be **dry-run-first** and carry a **hard `RAISE EXCEPTION` guard**\n  (pre + post); a read-only dry-run does NOT stop a wrong-DB `COMMIT` no-op.\n- In any `form_instances.data` fix, **sync the `versions[]` snapshot** in the same\n  script (set `versions[-1].data = data`), else the Version-History panel goes\n  stale and needs a second run.\n- Prod migration fixes: targeted SQL for prod, extractor + staging `--force` —\n  **not** a prod `--force` re-import.\n- Verify DB schema before raw SQL (entity `@Column({ name })` first); mind prod\n  `report_instances` schema drift.\n\n## Blast radius\n\n- A data ticket fixes only its named target; file a **separate Eng Backlog issue**\n  for the systemic code bug, with a full prod blast-radius table.\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/6-operations/browser-verification.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Browser Verification\n\nOwns **which tool drives a browser** for this repo, and the discipline that makes the\ndefault reliable. Local stack bring-up is\n[`run-local-stack`](../../skills/run-local-stack/SKILL.md); the local smoke-test\nrecipe is [`verify-local-app`](../../skills/verify-local-app/SKILL.md). This file\nowns only the routing decision.\n\n---\n\n## Must-not-miss (stated in full)\n\n### The default is the script harness, not the browser MCP tools\n\n**Every authenticated browser verification on `local` / `staging` / `qa` / `uat` runs\nthrough `scripts/cds-session.mjs`** (Playwright, tracked, signs itself in). Reach for\nthe `claude-in-chrome` MCP tools only for an explicit exception below, and **say which\none applies** when you do.\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/cds-session.mjs --list                                # 18 demo users\nnode scripts/cds-session.mjs --env staging --probe /dashboard      # LOOK before selecting\nnode scripts/cds-session.mjs --env qa --role \"City Staff\" --account \"City of Seattle\"\n```\n\nThis is not a style preference. The harness is ~10× faster per step, and it is the\nonly path that produces evidence automatically — screenshots per step, `FAIL-*.png`\non a throw, and console/page/network/HTTP≥400 into `diagnostics.json`, which is\nexactly what the QA-handoff rule requires anyway\n([pr-review-conventions](../3-workflow/pr-review-conventions.md)).\n\n### The exceptions — narrow, and they stay narrow\n\nUse `claude-in-chrome` **only** when one of these is true:\n\n1. **Production — interactive verification.** `scripts/cds-session.mjs` hard-refuses prod\n   (exit 2) and that must not be softened. Driving prod UI to _verify a fix_ is\n   human-driven: a human signs in and the agent drives the already-authenticated session.\n   See [production-hotfix-and-sql](production-hotfix-and-sql.md).\n\n   **Not the same thing as read-only prod data capture.** There is a separate, sanctioned\n   Playwright path for pulling V1↔V2 evidence out of prod —\n   `.claude/skills/v1-v2-data-loss-audit/capture-v2-prod.mjs.template`, driven by\n   [`prod-migration-issue`](../../../docs/runbooks/prod-migration-issue.md) with credentials\n   from `workspace/packages/.env`. That script is **read-only**, purpose-built for the\n   migration audit, and is **not** covered by this rule — do not re-route it through the\n   session harness (the harness refuses prod by design), and do not cite this rule to block\n   it. The distinction that matters: **capturing prod data is allowed; interacting with prod\n   to verify behaviour is not.**\n\n   **An exception exempts a script from the ROUTING decision only.** It does not exempt it\n   from being correct, and never from being checked — the sanctioned prod capture script was\n   found logging in with `fill()` against a React-controlled form, i.e. a silent no-op\n   (CDS-2028, [lesson #19](../../lessons-learned.md)). Repair such a script in place.\n\n2. **The operator's own logged-in Chrome profile** — anything behind their SSO\n   (Linear, Slack, the AWS console). The harness only knows CDS demo users.\n3. **The operator wants to interact in their own browser**, mid-flow, alongside you.\n   (If they only want to _watch_, that is `--headed`, not a reason to switch tools.)\n4. **GIF evidence for a Linear attachment**, for now — `gif_creator` has no harness\n   equivalent wired up yet. Playwright's `recordVideo` could take this over.\n\n\"It felt easier\" is not on the list. Neither is \"I already had a tab open.\"\n\n### Probe before you select — never guess a selector from component source\n\nRun `--probe <path>` first. It returns the page's visible interactive controls (tag,\nrole, `href`, `data-testid`, `aria-label`, text), the headings, a count of controls\nthat exist but are hidden, and a full-page screenshot. Write the selector from that\noutput.\n\nThree things it encodes, each from a real mistake:\n\n- **`networkidle` is not a readiness signal for this app.** It resolves while the page is\n  still a skeleton. The probe additionally waits for the app's loading indicators to clear\n  and reports `settled`. Before that it inventoried a mid-load dashboard and reported a\n  fraction of the controls — and the number looked entirely plausible, which is what makes\n  it dangerous. **If `settled` is false, say so; do not report the inventory as the page.**\n- **Control counts are a property of the account's DATA, not of the route.** The same\n  `--probe /dashboard` returns 15 controls for one user and 26 for another whose Pending\n  Tasks list is populated, because most of the extra links are per-row deep links to\n  report-instance UUIDs. Never quote a control count as a fact about a page — cite the\n  env + user you ran as. (See [lesson #19](../../lessons-learned.md) for the PR that quoted such a count as a\n  property of the route.)\n- **`--probe` reports `httpStatus`; check it.** A typo'd or permission-denied route used to\n  return `settled: true` with zero controls and exit 0, which reads as an authoritative\n  \"this page has no controls\" rather than \"that route 404s\". It now exits 1 on ≥400.\n\nThe viewport is pinned to 1440×900 for **determinism** — reproducible screenshots and\ncomparable runs, not because a smaller viewport hides the nav (an A/B refuted that; the\ncollapsed sidebar was the loading skeleton — [lesson #19](../../lessons-learned.md)).\n\n### `type()`, never `fill()`\n\n`#email` / `#password` are React-controlled. `fill()` sets the value without the events\nReact needs, so the submit handler sees empty fields and fires **no request at all** —\nno error, no console message, URL unchanged. Clicking submit after `fill()` is also a\nsilent no-op. The harness does this correctly; don't hand-roll a login.\n\n`cds-web/e2e/auth.setup.ts` still uses `fill()` **and hardcodes a live shared demo password**\n— a credential exposure in tracked source, pre-existing, tracked as **CDS-2023**\n([lesson #19](../../lessons-learned.md)). Do not copy the pattern; it is not an example.\n\n### `uat` has only the system-scoped demo users\n\n`system.admin` and `tech.support` only. uat is provisioned **like production**: 16 of\nthe 18 registry users are absent from its Cognito pool, and its accounts are Sunnyvale /\nSan Mateo / City of Salinas — **City of Seattle and King County do not exist there**.\nAccount/agency-scoped selections on uat are refused by the harness with an explanation.\nUse `local` / `staging` / `qa` for role-scoped verification.\n\nWorth knowing because of how this presents: Cognito answers a non-existent user with\n`NotAuthorizedException`, identical to a wrong password. A previous session spent real\ntime hunting a credential bug that did not exist. If a login fails on one env but works\non another for the same password, **check the user exists in that pool first**\n(`aws cognito-idp admin-get-user`).\n\n### No session caching — do not re-add it\n\nA `storageState` cache was built, measured, and removed (CDS-2019). The reasoning is\nrecorded in `scripts/cds-session.mjs`; the short version:\n\n- An API liveness check cannot distinguish a **dead** superseded session from a live one —\n  both return 200 — so a cached run reported success against a dead session, the worst\n  failure a verification harness can have. Only the app can tell them apart, which costs\n  about what a login costs; reuse was intermittent and the miss path was slower than no\n  cache. Measurements and post-mortem: [lesson #19](../../lessons-learned.md).\n\nEvery run logs in fresh. That is the intended design, not a missing optimisation.\n\n---\n\n## Credentials\n\nOne shared demo password for every non-prod env, resolved first-hit-wins:\n\n1. `$CDS_DEMO_PASSWORD`\n2. `--env-file <path>`\n3. `<repo>/.claude/skills/compare-v1-v2/.env`\n4. `~/.cds/demo.env` — **machine-level; the only one that survives a fresh worktree**\n\nAll are gitignored by design, which means tracking the harness did not make a fresh\ncheckout self-sufficient — the credential has to come from the machine-level path. Never\nhardcode it, never print it. Standing permission covers signing in on staging / qa / uat\nwith these demo accounts; driving **production** interactively stays human-only (the\nread-only prod capture script is the carve-out in exception 1).\n\nA fresh worktree also needs its dependencies: the harness imports `playwright`, which this\nmonorepo hoists to the **repo-root** `node_modules`. Without a root `npm install` (or the\nsymlink trick in [ports-and-local-artifacts](ports-and-local-artifacts.md)) it fails with a\nraw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack. \"Works in a fresh worktree\" means _no copy step_, not\n_no install_.\n\n## Never report \"blocked, needs a password\"\n\nLogging in is automated. If a verification cannot proceed, the reason is something else\n— say what it actually is, with the output\n([minimal-change-discipline](../2-engineering/minimal-change-discipline.md), and the\nno-verified-without-an-artifact rule).\n\n---\n\n_This rule qualifies on the **severity** axis of the\n[maintenance policy](../README.md#when-a-pattern-earns-a-rule-project-wide): the removed\nsession cache produced a run that reported success against a dead session, and the\n`--probe` skeleton bug produced a plausible-looking but wrong page inventory. Both are\nsilent-wrong-answer classes, which earn a rule on first occurrence._\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/6-operations/extractor-and-dashboard-deploys.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Extractor & Dashboard Deploys\n\nOwns **how V1-migration extractor code actually reaches a running environment**.\nDeploy paths for the app itself live in\n[production-hotfix-and-sql](production-hotfix-and-sql.md).\n\nLeft **unscoped** deliberately, and the reason generalises: `paths:` scoping keys\noff the files a session is **editing**, but this rule is needed when you are\n**operating** — merging someone else's dashboard PR, dispatching a build, or\nasking \"is my extractor change live?\". None of those edit a matching file, so a\n`paths:` glob would leave the rule absent at exactly the moment it applies.\n\nScope rules by **audience, not by size**: `paths:` for things you need while\nediting a specific area, unscoped for things you need while operating on the\nsystem. Note that **no rule file carries `paths:` frontmatter today** — the\nmechanism is verified to work, but there is no scoped precedent here to match, so\nthis is the frame for the decision rather than a description of the tree\n([README loading note](../README.md)).\n\n---\n\n## Must-not-miss (stated in full)\n\n### Merging a `cds-data-migration` PR deploys nothing, anywhere\n\nThat repo contains **one** workflow — `tests.yml`, pytest only. There is no\ndeploy workflow in it, for any environment. The extractor reaches an env only\nby being **baked into the migration-dashboard image at build time**:\n\n- `migration-dashboard/Dockerfile` — `COPY v1_data_migration_app/ /app/v1_migration/`\n- `.github/workflows/*migration-dashboard.yml` — `extra_checkout_repo: citydataservices/cds-data-migration`\n  checked out into `v1_data_migration_app`\n- `.github/workflows/shared-workflow.yml` — the two \"Checkout extra repository\" steps\n\nDashboard builds trigger only on **this** repo's paths (`migration-dashboard/**`,\n`cds-api/src/migration/**`, the workflow files) per env branch, or by dispatch:\n\n```bash\ngh workflow run migration-dashboard.yml     --ref main   # staging (no inputs)\ngh workflow run qa-migration-dashboard.yml  --ref qa -f version_tag=1.0.0   # input required, ignored\n```\n\nStaging does not set `check_ecr_first`, so a dispatch genuinely rebuilds (it\noverwrites the same nbgv tag with new content) and then rolls the service\n(`wait-for-service-stability: true`).\n\n### The cross-repo checkout resolves differently per event — three consequences, all silent\n\n`shared-workflow.yml` has **two** cross-repo checkout steps, and which one runs\ndepends on the event:\n\n| Step | Guard | `ref:` |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| \"Checkout extra repository (matching branch)\" | `github.head_ref != ''` — i.e. `pull_request` only; `continue-on-error` | `ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}` — **pinned** to the same-named branch |\n| \"Checkout extra repository (default branch)\" | `head_ref == ''` (push / dispatch) or the matching step failed | none — **default-branch tip at build time** |\n\nSo on push and `workflow_dispatch` the extractor version inside an image is\ndecided by *build timing*, not by anything recorded in either repo's history:\n\n- **An unrelated dashboard merge ships your extractor change.** Any\n  `migration-dashboard/**` or `cds-api/src/migration/**` merge rebuilds the image\n  and picks up whatever is on `cds-data-migration` `main` right then — including\n  commits nobody in that PR knows about, at a time nobody associates with them.\n  Never reason \"I did not dispatch, so it is not deployed.\"\n- **Images are not reproducible.** Rebuilding the same `cds-app-rewrite` SHA twice\n  can bake different extractor code.\n- **CI validates one extractor version and the deploy ships another.** On a\n  dashboard **PR** run the first step fires, so a same-named branch in\n  `cds-data-migration` is what CI builds against (PR runs do build — `SHOULD_DEPLOY`\n  gates only the deploy). Merge the PR and the post-merge build takes `main`'s tip\n  instead. Green CI on a dashboard PR is therefore not evidence about the artifact\n  that will be deployed.\n\n**Therefore: never infer the deployed extractor version from either repo's git\nlog — verify what is running.** After merging a `cds-data-migration` PR, either\ndispatch the build deliberately, or check the live task; and when reviewing a\ndashboard PR, remember its image will also carry the extractor's current tip.\n\nThe build itself already records the answer. `shared-workflow.yml`'s \"Log extra\ncheckout ref\" step prints the resolved `cds-data-migration` SHA into every build\nlog, which is the cheapest possible check — no AWS calls, no inference:\n\n```bash\ngh run view <run-id> --log | grep -A2 'Drift-check extra repo'\n# a0df3be9...  Drift-check extra repo at a0df3be grafted, HEAD -> main, origin/main CDS-2083: ... (#61)\n```\n\nPair it with the running task's image **digest** (not its tag — env tags like\n`:qa` are overwritten in place, so the tag is stable across content changes):\n\n```bash\naws ecs describe-tasks --cluster platform --tasks <arn> \\\n  --query 'tasks[0].containers[?name==`qa-migration-dashboard`].imageDigest'\n```\n\nThis is the same failure class as CDS-1071's `:latest` (image content decoupled\nfrom the ref that names it), which is why it earns a rule on first statement\nrather than on recurrence.\n\n### A Terraform apply does not roll the dashboard service\n\n`modules/ecs-alb-service` sets `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [task_definition,\ndesired_count] }` — \"updated by CI/CD on every image push\". An apply registers\nrevision N+1 with the new env while the service keeps running N, reporting\n`rolloutState: COMPLETED`. That is designed.\n\n`force-new-deployment` does **not** fix it either: the pin means the forced\ndeployment restarts the task on the *same* revision (observed: applied 44, task\ncame up on 43). Make a task-definition change live by re-dispatching the deploy\nworkflow (it reads LATEST and registers N+1), or by naming the revision\nexplicitly:\n\n```bash\naws ecs update-service --task-definition <family>:<N> --force-new-deployment\n```\n\nVerify by reading back `tasks[0].taskDefinitionArn` — not the service's\n`rolloutState`, and not \"Apply complete\".\n\n---\n\n_Qualifies on the **severity** axis of the\n[maintenance policy](../README.md#when-a-pattern-earns-a-rule-project-wide): an\nunpinned cross-repo checkout ships unreviewed code into an environment silently,\nand the `ignore_changes` pin has twice produced a \"deployed\" claim that was\nfalse. Both are silent-wrong-answer classes._\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/2-engineering/recurring-review-patterns.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Recurring Review Patterns (Code Style)\n\nDistilled, codifiable do/don't rules extracted from review comments that keep\nrecurring across PRs. This is the **style layer** — terse rules with tiny\nexamples. The war-story detail lives in [`../../lessons-learned.md`](../../lessons-learned.md);\ncross-references point there. When a rule here is violated in review, cite it by\nits heading instead of re-explaining.\n\n> Scope: `cds-api` (NestJS) + `cds-web` (React/Next). Owns _repeat_ correctness/\n> type/test/idiom feedback. Keep minimal and non-overlapping — if a pattern is\n> already a full lesson, link it, don't restate it.\n\n---\n\n## Data correctness\n\n### 1. Clear an optional field with `null`, never `undefined`\n\nThe Program-style save path is a **full-object PATCH**: the FE builds the whole\nDTO, `axios` `JSON.stringify` **drops `undefined` keys**, and the service applies\nfields under an `Object.hasOwn(dto, key)` guard, persisting via TypeORM\n`manager.save(entity)` — which **skips `undefined` properties** (leaves the column\nunchanged). Net effect: setting a saved optional field back to blank with\n`undefined` is silently a no-op — the old value stays in the DB.\n\n- **FE** — send `null` on clear so the key survives serialization:\n  `heroNumber: formData.heroNumber ?? null` (not `|| undefined`).\n- **Service** — write the `null` through: `program.heroNumber = dto.heroNumber || null`\n  (not `dto.heroNumber ?? undefined`). `|| null` also normalizes `\"\"` → `NULL`.\n- **Types** — the column/DTO/FE type is `T | null` end-to-end (see #6).\n\n`contractNumber` still has this latent bug; don't copy it. (CDS-975 heroNumber.)\n\n### 2. Never let `||` collapse a falsy-but-valid value\n\n`false`, `0`, and `\"\"` are real values, not \"unset\". `value || fallback` throws\nthem away.\n\n- Use `??` for defaulting; assign booleans **straight through**\n  (`program.x = dto.x`, not `dto.x || false` — that turns an explicit **No** into\n  the default).\n- The one intentional exception is the clear-normalization in #1 (`|| null` to\n  fold `\"\"`→`NULL`) — that's deliberate, comment it.\n- **Test the `false`/`0`/`\"\"` case**, not just the truthy happy value (see #8).\n\n### 3. Don't implicitly hide null/blank in the UI — render an explicit em-dash\n\nNever `{value && <Field/>}`. Render the row unconditionally with an explicit\nplaceholder: `value ?? \"—\"`, or for tri-state booleans\n`x === true ? \"Yes\" : x === false ? \"No\" : \"Not specified\"`. Hiding on null makes\na real \"empty\" indistinguishable from \"not rendered.\" (memory:\nno-implicit-field-hiding.)\n\n**Sanctioned exception — owner-specified hide-when-empty.** The em-dash is the\ndefault, but when the product owner explicitly specifies that a read-only section\nshould _hide_ empty fields (e.g. CDS-976 contact-info: hide each empty field and\nthe whole block when all are empty), that override is allowed. Call it out in the\nPR body so a reviewer doesn't cite this rule as a bug. This is the read-only\ndisplay only — edit forms still show every control.\n\n### 4. Equality / change-detection compares the full breakdown, not an aggregate\n\nAny `xEqual` / `normalizeX` / snapshot-compare must key on **every contributing\nfield**, never a derived sum/total — an offsetting redistribution that preserves\nthe total would read as \"unchanged\" and skip an amendment or bypass a guard.\nFull detail: [lesson #17](../../lessons-learned.md).\n\n---\n\n## Wiring completeness\n\n### 5. A new persisted field must reach EVERY reader and writer\n\nAdding one field is a checklist, not one edit. Grep an existing sibling field name\n(`contractNumber`, `cdbgCategory`) to find all the sites, then cover:\n\n- [ ] entity `@Column` + a `Date.now()`-timestamped migration (both up/down)\n- [ ] create-map (the `manager.save(Program, {...})` object)\n- [ ] update-whitelist (`if (Object.hasOwn(dto, \"x\")) program.x = ...`)\n- [ ] read DTO / serializer (`ReadProgramDto`)\n- [ ] FE types — **all** of `Program`, `CreateProgramRequest`, `ProgramFormData`\n- [ ] edit form control **and** the read-only view surface\n- [ ] `cds-api/swagger-spec.json` regenerated (see #7)\n- [ ] downstream exports (CAPER / IDIS / full-data-report) — wire them or\n      **explicitly** confirm out of scope in the PR\n\nA superseding field additionally has to update every reader of the **old** field\n— `tsc` won't catch readers behind `any`/casts, so grep. ([lesson #17](../../lessons-learned.md).)\n\n### 6. Match nullable typing end-to-end — don't launder it through `any`\n\nIf a column is nullable/clearable, type it `T | null` from entity → DTO → FE.\nCasts (`x as any`, `: any`) blind `tsc` to shape changes (required→optional,\nnew nullability), so the break only shows at runtime as a silent `$0`/blank.\n([lesson #17](../../lessons-learned.md).)\n\n### 7. Regenerate `swagger-spec.json` when you touch `@ApiProperty` DTOs\n\n`cds-api/swagger-spec.json` is a **committed artifact with no CI regen** — stale\nspecs drift silently. Run `npm run --prefix cds-api swagger:spec` (needs a\nDB-connected env) and commit the diff in the same PR. The generator only emits the\nTS-inferred `type` + `@ApiProperty` fields — it ignores class-validator\ndecorators, so the diff is deterministic.\n\n---\n\n## Validation & types\n\n### 8. Test the adversarial shape, not the happy path\n\nFor every field/aggregate, the test that matters is the empty / zero / `false` /\ncleared / multi-element case:\n\n- A single control over an array must **read and write the whole array**, and be\n  tested with populated multi-element data — not the easy zero/single case.\n- Green tests on a **seeded** account prove nothing about the configurable\n  (dynamic-nanoid-id) case — the seed-masking trap. ([lesson #16](../../lessons-learned.md);\n  memory: aggregate-input-and-adversarial-tests.)\n\n### 9. DTO validation mirrors the DB constraint\n\n`varchar(N)` → `@MaxLength(N)`; numeric-string → `@Matches(/^\\d*$/)`; enum →\n`@IsEnum`. Defense-in-depth for non-UI API callers, and a clean `400` instead of a\nraw Postgres error. Never hand-type a migration timestamp — use `Date.now()` /\n`migration:create` ([lesson #2](../../lessons-learned.md)).\n\n---\n\n## NestJS / React idioms\n\n### 10. Mark React component props `Readonly<>`\n\nEvery component's props type is `Readonly<Props>` (Sonar S6759). Match the file's\nexisting tab/section components rather than leaving one bare.\n\n### 11. Never swallow an error in a bare `catch`\n\nA `catch` that returns a default / empty with no re-throw and no diagnostic hides\nplausible-but-wrong behavior. Throw with full context, or log-and-rethrow — no\nsilent fallbacks. ([lesson #12](../../lessons-learned.md); memory: no-silent-fallbacks.)\n\n### 12. New constructor dep ⇒ update the spec's providers\n\nWhen a PR adds a constructor parameter to an `@Injectable`, its `*.spec.ts`\n`Test.createTestingModule({ providers: [...] })` must add a matching mock, or\n`compile()` throws `Nest can't resolve dependencies …` and the whole suite goes\nred. Grep the changed service's spec for the new dep.\n\n### 13. Don't hardcode `formData` field-id keys\n\nReading another field via a literal id (`formData[\"expense-summary-container\"]`)\nonly works for **seeded** templates; Form-Builder templates use nanoid ids, so the\nlookup silently misses. Pass the real field id in as a prop. ([lesson #16](../../lessons-learned.md).)\n\n### 14. Don't pile new branches into already-complex service methods\n\n`createDraft`/`updateDraft`-style methods already exceed Sonar's cognitive-\ncomplexity threshold (S3776). Adding a field to their whitelist pattern is fine\n(no new branching), but do **not** introduce new nested conditionals there —\nextract a helper, or (matching `ProgramForm.tsx`/`reports.service.ts` precedent)\nadd a scoped S3776 suppression rather than letting complexity climb. Sonar red is\nnon-blocking for merge, but new smells still shouldn't be authored.\n\n---\n\n---\n\n## Security\n\n### 15. Client-side RBAC is not a security control — mirror it server-side\n\nThe single most-repeated security comment (**#1060, #1062, #1080, #1090, #1107**).\nA permission/role matrix implemented only as a UI helper (`canEditCityContacts`,\nhidden fields, disabled buttons, or a `sanitizeAgencyAdminLiveProgramUpdate` that\nstrips _some_ fields) is **not** enforcement: a caller with the coarse write\npermission (`update:programs`) can still PATCH the fields the UI hides. Every\nfield-level or action-level restriction shown in the UI must be mirrored by a\nserver-side check on the corresponding write endpoint.\n\nSharpened corollary to [lesson #5](../../lessons-learned.md): a boolean helper\nnamed `hasAgencyRole()` / `hasXRole()` with **no `accountId`/`agencyId` filter**,\nreused as a fallback inside `ensureCanRead*`/`ensureCanWrite*`, is an IDOR — it\nanswers \"does this user have the role _anywhere_,\" not \"on _this_ tenant.\" Join to\nthe tenant id; don't scope-check with a global role boolean. (Recurred near-verbatim\nacross ~9 PRs — the dominant review theme overall.)\nSee [rbac-and-authz-scoping](../5-security/rbac-and-authz-scoping.md).\n\n## Accessibility\n\n### 16. New interactive / animated UI needs a11y baked in\n\n**5 PRs** (#975, #976, #1054, #1059, #1123). The project has **zero**\n`prefers-reduced-motion` usage today, so every new animation reintroduces the gap.\n\n- New interactive controls: explicit `role` + `aria-*` (a progress bar needs\n  `role=\"progressbar\"` + `aria-valuenow/min/max`; an editable `<input>` needs a\n  `<label htmlFor>` or `aria-label`).\n- New CSS transitions/animations: a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` fallback.\n- Keyboard focus must not rely on color alone — don't `outline-none` without a\n  visible non-color focus indicator.\n\n## Testing (continued from #8)\n\n### 17. Every new method ships with its tests in the same PR — authz methods especially\n\nThe **most-recurring engineering comment** (~9 PRs: #978, #979, #980, #1018–#1021,\n#1088, #1079). A green `tsc` is not coverage. Any new method needs unit tests in\nthe same PR; a new **security-critical** method (role/scope check) needs, at\nminimum: the **allow** case, the **deny** case, and the **boundary/empty** case\n(e.g. `AgencyAdmin → true`, `AgencyStaff → false`, `no role → false`).\n\n## Workflow hygiene\n\n### 18. Backport / cherry-pick PRs carry the regression test too\n\n**3 PRs** (#1071, #1072, #1105). When porting a fix to `uat`/`production`, port the\naccompanying `*.spec.ts` changes with the production code — don't ship the fix\nwithout its test. If the harness on that branch has diverged so the test can't\ncompile, **say so explicitly in the PR body** rather than silently dropping it.\nExtends [production-hotfix-and-sql](../6-operations/production-hotfix-and-sql.md).\n\n### 19. No debug `console.log` in the diff\n\n**3 PRs** (#1019, #1021, #1036 — one logged user email/roleId/permissionIds). Grep\nthe diff for `console.log` before requesting review; always remove before merge.\n\n### 20. Don't bundle unrelated `swagger-spec.json` endpoints into a PR\n\nBorderline (**#1036, #1040**) but a clean corollary to the \"no unrelated files\"\nrule: after regenerating the spec (#7), grep the swagger diff for endpoints with no\ncorresponding controller change in the same PR — a regen off a stale local branch\nsweeps in others' unrelated endpoints.\n\n### 21. Shared modules & core entities must stay backward compatible — verify the legacy path\n\nProduction runs live `Program`s (and their budget / revenue-source / expense / goals /\ncontacts sub-entities, plus reports and application instances) in the **legacy**\nshape. Any change to a **shared module** or a **shared / core entity** MUST leave\nexisting records rendering, validating, and persisting **exactly as before** — and\nthat has to be verified on the **legacy** path, because new-shape / seeded tests pass\nregardless (the seed/legacy-masking trap, cf. [lessons #7 / #16 / #17](../../lessons-learned.md)).\n\n- **Legacy render/validate/persist unchanged.** Trace a pre-existing legacy record\n  through the changed code; confirm identical output — no `$0`/empty, no new\n  validation rejection, no dropped field.\n- **Detect \"new shape\" by an explicit opt-in, never an incidental property.** Gating\n  new behavior on \"an `id` is present\" / \"a map exists\" / \"a flag is set\" misfires on\n  every adjacent flow that already set that property for another reason.\n  - **Enforcement — enumerate every WRITER of the property, and read each one.** The\n    principle above is not self-checking: you cannot know a property is a valid\n    discriminator until you have listed everything that sets it. Grep the property\n    name across `cds-api` **and** `cds-web`, and for each writer answer _\"could this\n    produce the gated shape without meaning to?\"_ One writer is never the answer —\n    there are two editors (program + application/template) for most of these concepts.\n    Checking a single writer and generalizing is the specific mistake this bullet\n    exists to stop (CDS-1727 round 2: \"no product flow produces a zero-`isMain`\n    budget\" was asserted from `BudgetTab` alone; the _application_ revenue table\n    defaults `isMain: false` on every row, so the state was reachable and money was\n    lost). Applies to the **author** as much as the reviewer — see\n    [`self-review/SKILL.md`](../../skills/self-review/SKILL.md).\n  - **Confirm the storage shape before reasoning about ORM behavior.** Run\n    `\\d <table>` (or read the entity's `@Column`) and check whether the sub-entity is\n    a real table or an embedded `jsonb` column. They behave nothing alike: a table row\n    gets a generated PK, an embedded jsonb object gets only the fields the mapper\n    assigned. Assuming the former for the latter inverts your conclusion about whether\n    a discriminator is even present (CDS-1727: `budgets.revenue_sources` is `jsonb`,\n    so converted programs carry **no** source ids — the opposite of the assumption).\n- **One shared accessor** for a field with sibling representations (extends #4/#5), so\n  every reader — viewers, reports, exports, PDF/agreement templates, completeness/\n  submission gates, change-detection, **and both editors** — is correct by default.\n- **Ship a legacy regression test** that loads a pre-existing legacy record and asserts\n  unchanged behavior; its absence on a shared/core-entity change is itself a finding.\n\nA demonstrated legacy break is a **Bug (backward-compat regression)**, production-critical.\n(CDS-1727: `revenueSourcesHaveStableIds` flipped the application editor to the new\nper-source shape while the legacy-field mirror was program-only, so legacy/app budgets\nread `$0`; the new per-source `validateOrThrow` also threw when reached via\n`applyRevision`→`rebalanceRevenueSources`.) The review-time discovery method is the\n**Shared-Surface Side-Effect Scan** in\n[`pr-review/SKILL.md`](../../skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) Step 3.4.\n\nThis **generalizes rules #4/#5** (change-detection + superseding-field wiring — the\nwar story behind them is [lesson #17](../../lessons-learned.md)) from a single field to\nany shared module or core entity, and extends their shared-accessor requirement to the\nlegacy path — treat **rule #5** as the field-level case and #21 as the\nmodule/entity-level case; keep them cross-linked, don't fork the guidance. This rule qualifies on the **severity** axis of\nthe maintenance policy below (not recurrence): a backward-compat regression on a\nshared/core entity is production-critical, and CDS-1727 alone produced multiple such\nbreaks across separate readers — a critical class earns a rule on first occurrence.\n\n## Layout\n\n### 22. Hiding a cell in a positional grid reflows every cell after it\n\nA multi-column grid whose children are rendered conditionally, with no explicit\n`grid-column`, silently reflows: removing one cell pulls every later sibling back a slot.\nWhere the grid encodes an **intended pairing** (`Contact | Email`, `Address | Contract #`),\na value lands under the wrong heading. A `col-span-N` item that no longer fits in the\ncolumns left on its row is pushed down, opening a blank half-row above it.\n\n**The trigger is narrow — all three must hold:**\n\n1. an `&&` conditional child (a ternary always renders something, so no slot is vacated);\n2. **siblings after it** (a conditional last child shifts nothing);\n3. the grid **encodes intended column positions** — signalled by `col-span-N` on some\n   children, a comment naming rows/pairs, or V1 parity. A flow list laid out 2-up has no\n   intended pairing and reflows harmlessly (`ReportInstanceView.tsx:720` has eight\n   conditional children and is fine).\n\n**Sanctioned fixes.** The codebase held three of these independently before anyone\nnoticed they were the same problem; a fourth was added by CDS-976. Pick by shape:\n\n| Fix | Use when | Precedent |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Hold the slot with an empty cell | a partner cell must keep its column | `template-budget-revision-report` `HeaderField` |\n| Render nothing but keep the wrapper | the wrapper carries the `col-span` | `template-expense-header-info` address cells |\n| Vary the column count | hiding a cell should re-balance the row | `template-budget-revenue-sources` (`grid-cols-3` ↔ `grid-cols-2`) |\n| Guard the whole row | the entire row is empty and should vanish | `ContactInfoForm`, `template-qpr-header-info` Row 6 |\n\nRestoring a placeholder value is **not** one of them where a hide-when-empty rule applies\n(CDS-976 AC7) — hold the slot and render nothing inside it.\n\n**Assert it mechanically; the usual assertions are blind to it.** `queryByText(\"Contact\")`\nand \"no em-dash remains\" both pass while the layout is wrong. Use\n`cds-web/test-utils/grid-layout.ts` — it re-implements CSS Grid auto-placement over DOM\norder and `col-span-*` classes (jsdom does no layout, so measuring is not available) and\nreports both wrong-column cells and wide cells bumped to a new row:\n\n```ts\nexpectGridColumns(container.querySelector(\".md\\\\:grid-cols-2\"), {\n  Agency: 0, \"Project ID\": 1, Contact: 0, Email: 1,\n});\n```\n\nPrefer a property test over every empty/populated combination to a test per reported case\n— see the war story below for why.\n\n**Why this is a rule (severity axis).** CDS-976 shipped `Contact: —` to production. The\nfirst fix addressed the reported cell; round 2 found the identical defect on a sibling\nheader and fixed it there; round 3 (Anish, PR #1384) found it *again* on the component the\nprod ticket was actually filed against. Three rounds, each narrower than the defect,\nbecause each was scoped to what someone had observed. A 32-combination property test then\nreported **64** violations against the pre-fix component rather than the one reported —\nemptying `address` alone shifted four fields and pushed both `col-span-2` totals mid-row.\nConfirmed in Chromium on staging: removing the Contact cell moved Email from x=854 to\nx=341. Round 1 had also seen the reflow and dismissed it as cosmetic, arguing a\nslot-holding cell was \"exactly what AC7 forbids\" — wrong, because AC7 forbids a visible\nplaceholder and an empty shell renders nothing.\n\nRelated: this is the layout-level sibling of #3 (no implicit field hiding). #3 governs\n*whether* a field renders; this governs what happens to its neighbours when it does not.\n\n---\n\n---\n\n_Maintenance: a pattern earns a rule on **recurrence** (3+ PRs) **or severity** (a\nsingle production-critical incident) — the project-wide policy is in\n[`README.md`](../README.md#when-a-pattern-earns-a-rule-project-wide); most rules here\nqualify on recurrence (see the \"recurred across ~N PRs\" callouts), #21 and #22 on severity.\nOne rule = one heading; when it changes, edit the heading, don't fork it._\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/2-engineering/minimal-change-discipline.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Code Changes\n\n- Prefer the **minimal fix** that addresses the specific request. Do NOT refactor\n  or modify unrelated files.\n- If a change touches **more than 3–4 files, pause and confirm scope** with the\n  user before proceeding.\n- When fixing build/test errors, fix **ALL** errors in a single pass. Scan the\n  full output; do not stop after the first failure.\n- Read relevant code sections **before** editing; preserve existing functionality.\n- **Never break type safety.** Maintain proper error handling.\n- **No silent fallbacks** — throw with full context; don't return empty/defaults.\n- **No implicit field hiding when data is null** — render an explicit em-dash\n  \"—\"; never `{value && <Field/>}`.\n- Don't claim \"verified\" without running the code end-to-end (lesson #7).\n\n## Observe the system; don't model it\n\nThe dominant authoring failure is a confident belief about a data shape that a\nfew seconds of looking would have falsified. Before reasoning about behaviour:\n\n- **Look at the stored shape, not the type.** `\\d <table>` / the entity's\n  `@Column({ name })`. An embedded `jsonb` sub-entity is not a table row — it has\n  no generated PK and carries only the fields the mapper set.\n- **Look at the writers, not just the readers.** Grep every site that sets the\n  field, repo-wide, and read each. A reader sweep answers \"who breaks?\"; only a\n  writer sweep answers \"can this state even occur?\" (Enforcement detail:\n  [recurring-review-patterns #21](recurring-review-patterns.md).)\n- **Look for the same problem already solved.** Before writing a classifier,\n  predicate, or normalizer, grep the ticket ID and the concept — the other side\n  of the stack may already have a hardened version with the trap documented in\n  a comment. Reuse it; a weaker duplicate is worse than no abstraction.\n\n## A rescue net means the design is wrong\n\nIf a fix needs a compat net, fallback branch, or \"rescue\" to stop an adjacent\ncase from breaking, **stop and redesign** — do not add the net. Nets compose\nbadly: each one creates a new interaction with the last, and the second one\nalmost always reintroduces the first one's bug in a new place.\n\nThe correct shape is usually: **prove the new-shape preconditions once,\nconservatively; otherwise fall back whole to the legacy path** — which by\nconstruction still has somewhere to put every legacy field. If you cannot state\nthe preconditions as an explicit list, you do not yet understand the data.\n\n(CDS-1727: two rounds of patching compat nets produced three new bugs —\ndouble-counted totals, unreachable-state money loss, all-`$0` cells. Replacing\nboth nets with a four-condition `isProven…` predicate fixed all three.)\n\n### The same failure at PR scale — round N fixing round N−1 is a split signal\n\nThe rule above is about a line of code; it applies unchanged to a **pull request**. When a review\nround's findings are bugs introduced by the _previous_ round's fixes, the PR has become the\ncompat net: each fix creates a new interaction with the last, in a different file.\n\n**The trigger is mechanical — stop and split when either holds:**\n\n- a review round finds a defect **in code added by an earlier round of the same PR**; or\n- the diff crosses the **3–4 file gate** while you are fixing review findings rather than\n  building the feature.\n\nSplitting means: land the independently-verified parts (each with its own tests) as their own PRs,\nand keep the contested core alone where a reviewer can hold all of it in their head. Do **not**\nrespond by reviewing harder — that is the net. (CDS-1183: four review rounds, seven confirmed\nbugs, **five of them authored by earlier rounds of the same PR**, ending at 13 files across five\nconcerns. Rounds 3 and 4 each found bugs in the round that preceded them.)\n\nCorollary for cost: fanning more reviewers at a PR in this state is the expensive way to discover\nit needs splitting. Review breadth pays on round 1 and decays fast after it — measured on\nCDS-1183 round 4, three parallel reviewers cost ~676k tokens for **4** unique findings, with a\nquarter of the output re-reporting already-fixed items.\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/2-engineering/template-field-conventions.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Template & Form Builder Conventions\n\n- **Config ↔ UI parity (hard rule):** every config option on a template field\n  (e.g. `showJurisdiction`, `showTotalRow`, `incomeTableLayout`) MUST have a\n  matching UI control in the field's properties panel\n  (`field-properties/Qpr*Properties.tsx`). Never add a config-only option without\n  a toggle/input in the template editor.\n\n- **No hardcoded `formData` field keys** — they break Form-Builder (dynamic-id)\n  templates; only seeded literal-id templates work (lesson #16).\n\n- To pass context/handlers to template fields via `formData`: register the key in\n  `READ_ONLY_METADATA_FIELDS` **and** both save skip-lists, or functions get\n  `String()`-ified.\n\n- A new field that supersedes an existing one must update **every reader** of the\n  old field, and change-detection must compare the breakdown, not the total\n  (lesson #17).\n\n- **Verifying a template/component feature — decide config-gated vs unconditional\n  first, then pick the right template to test on.** Before capturing evidence for a\n  report-template/component change, determine whether the feature needs a\n  **component config/property to be set** to activate (e.g. `includeCityUseOnly`,\n  `showTotalRow`) or renders **unconditionally** (hardcoded in the component,\n  every account):\n  - **Config-gated** → verify on a **newly-created** report template with the\n    property set via the field-properties panel — **not** a pre-seeded live\n    template. The seed/bootstrap re-sync may already carry the config, masking\n    whether a fresh (Form-Builder / new-account) template actually works\n    (seed-masking trap, lesson #16). Confirm the config↔UI toggle exists too.\n  - **Unconditional (all accounts)** → the live seeded template is representative,\n    but still confirm on a **second account** so \"renders everywhere\" isn't assumed\n    from one tenant. The\n> `issue-investigator` / `issue-planner` / `issue-implementer` / `staging-verifier`\n> workflow is local-only (its agents and playbook are excluded from git), so its\n> mechanics — investigation verdicts, wave scheduling, the human digest — live in\n> `docs/playbooks/multi-agent-issue-to-pr-workflow.md` beside the agents that\n> implement them, not here. Documenting them in a tracked, always-loaded rule\n> charged every teammate's session for a workflow none of them can run.\n\n> Scope: this rule owns the **orchestration invariants** — concurrency, ordering,\n> and the outward-action gate. Per-issue code discipline still comes from\n> [minimal-change-discipline](../2-engineering/minimal-change-discipline.md),\n> [recurring-review-patterns](../2-engineering/recurring-review-patterns.md), and\n> [rbac-and-authz-scoping](../5-security/rbac-and-authz-scoping.md). Branch/commit\n> safety comes from\n> [git-branch-and-commit-safety](git-branch-and-commit-safety.md).\n\n---\n\n## Must-not-miss (stated in full)\n\n### 1. No outward action autonomously — this is the human-in-the-loop gate\n\nSub-agents **prepare** outward actions and stop; a single human-gated step commits\nthem. \"Prepare, don't commit\" applies to **all** of:\n\n- opening / pushing a PR\n- moving a Linear status\n- posting Linear comments\n- merging, self-approving, deleting\n- any prod/uat-targeting PR, permission/RBAC change, or spend\n\nAn implementer's job ends at \"branch pushed to a fork/worktree + PR body drafted +\nfindings ready.\" The gate (a human, or the main loop with explicit approval)\ncommits them. Never auto-merge. Never self-approve (use `COMMENT` on your own PR).\n\n### 2. One issue = one worktree; never touch the shared primary tree\n\nEach implementer runs in its **own** `git worktree` off the latest base\n(`isolation: worktree`). It must **never** `checkout` / `switch` / `reset --hard`\n/ `stash` the shared primary working tree — another session may be using it.\nRe-verify the branch (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`) **after** entering the\nworktree and **before** the first edit. After any implementer run, the primary\ntree's checked-out branch must be unchanged — assert this.\n\n### 3. File-overlap = serialize\n\nThe planner must not run two implementers on overlapping files/subsystems\nconcurrently — that produces merge conflicts or silent supersession. Independent\nissues fan out; issues that share files (or a Linear `blockedBy`, or migration\nordering) run **serially**, and the dependent rebases onto its blocker **after the\nblocker merges** — not off a stale base.\n\n### 4. Verify-before-implement\n\nNo implementer spawns until the gap is **confirmed real**, checked against\n**`origin/main` AND the target deploy branch** — never one branch, and never a\nstale local tree. Overstating a gap is the marquee failure mode (CDS-981); a\nsingle-branch grep is not verification. If the gap turns out to be already fixed,\nskip it; if it needs a human answer or a scope call, hold that issue and escalate\nit alone rather than guessing into code.\n\n---\n\n## Concurrency / git\n\n- **Dedup before planning, and AGAIN immediately before any push / PR-open.** An\n  issue may already have a branch/PR (#1133), and a parallel gate may have pushed\n  your exact commit and opened the PR while you worked (#1143). Re-run\n  `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` right before the outward action; if a PR\n  exists at your head SHA, **report and stop** — do not re-push or re-create.\n- **Stale base** — branch every worktree off the _latest_ base; rebase dependents\n  after their blocker merges.\n- **Migrations via `migration:create` only** — never hand-type a timestamp prefix;\n  two agents hand-typing collide (and fail `validate-migration-filenames.sh`). See\n  [migration-authoring-and-validation](../4-data/migration-authoring-and-validation.md).\n- **One consolidated comment per ticket, edited in place** — N agents each posting\n  is comment sprawl. **Sub-agents return conclusions** (verdict + plan + file:line),\n  not file dumps, so the orchestrator's context does not blow up.\n\nEach sub-agent remains bound by the ordinary authoring rules — no \"verified\"\nwithout an executed artifact, minimal scope with the 3–4 file gate, and a new\nmethod/endpoint ships its tests and its scope check\n([minimal-change-discipline](../2-engineering/minimal-change-discipline.md),\n[recurring-review-patterns](../2-engineering/recurring-review-patterns.md) #15/#17).\nBeing a sub-agent grants no exemption; restating each rule here only let the two\ncopies drift.\n\nThree obligations are **specific to delegation** and are stated here because no\nother rule owns them:\n\n- **Separate your errors from pre-existing ones.** A sub-agent reports into a\n  context that cannot see its shell. \"Tests fail\" without that split makes the\n  orchestrator debug the wrong diff.\n- **File a separate issue for adjacent gaps** rather than widening the diff — the\n  3–4 file gate is what the sub-agent trips instead of quietly absorbing the gap.\n- **Don't over-ask.** Investigator questions are only for what code and data\n  cannot answer; a question answerable from the codebase is a defect, not a\n  question. Escalation is expensive precisely because it costs a human turn.\n\n## Not parallelizable (serialize or escalate)\n\n- **Staging/browser verification** — one browser session. The `staging-verifier`\n  owns it and runs **serial**; the planner queues requests to it.\n- **Judgment** — spec interpretation, scope calls, low-confidence gaps → escalate\n  to a human; never silently guess into code.\n\n---\n\n## Review fan-out — breadth decays after round 1\n\nFanning several reviewers at one PR buys **breadth of perspective**, which is worth a lot on the\nfirst pass and very little on the fourth. Measured on CDS-1183 round 4 (three parallel reviewers:\n`pr-review`, an AC/QA reviewer, and a side-effect skeptic):\n\n|           | Tokens    | Wall clock | Unique actionable findings |\n| --------- | --------- | ---------- | -------------------------- |\n| pr-review | 274k      | 17 min     | **3** (both hard bugs)     |\n| skeptic   | 243k      | 21 min     | 1                          |\n| AC/QA     | 158k      | 8 min      | 1                          |\n| **total** | **~676k** | ~21 min    | **4**                      |\n\n≈170k tokens per finding, and roughly a quarter of the output was noise: three already-fixed items\nre-reported, one stale observation, one wrong severity, one wrong framing. An earlier round also\nproduced a false CRITICAL that the same agent later retracted in full.\n\n**Rules:**\n\n- **Round 1: fan out. Round ≥2: `pr-review` alone.** It found both of round 4's real bugs while the\n  other two cost ~400k tokens for two findings.\n- **Scope every review prompt to `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>..HEAD`, not the whole PR.** An\n  explicit \"already fixed, do not re-report\" list _demonstrably does not work_ — settled items came\n  back anyway. Don't show reviewers settled code.\n- **Prefer a deterministic check to an agent.** Most of what the skeptic contributed was\n  _discipline_, not intelligence: enumerate every writer, query the real stored shape, probe\n  fail-then-pass. Those are `rg`/`psql`/jest commands that run in seconds and are more reliable —\n  they corrected the reviewers' own severity claim. Run them yourself; see the Mechanical Claim\n  Checks in [`self-review`](../../skills/self-review/SKILL.md).\n- **Self-review before spawning anything.** Several round-4 findings were own-goals a careful pass\n  catches free: a test asserting the wrong element, a comment asserting an unverified writer, an\n  unreachable error render.\n- **Reviewer output is a claim, not a fact.** Verify before acting: in one round the severity\n  (\"every Sunnyvale program\") was wrong (3 of 89 budgets, Sunnyvale 0 of 82), and one agent\n  conflated two different column shapes. Check, then fix.\n\n**Root cause, stated plainly:** review cost is downstream of authoring quality and PR size. If\nround N keeps finding bugs from round N−1, more reviewers is the expensive way to learn the PR\nneeds splitting — see\n[minimal-change-discipline](../2-engineering/minimal-change-discipline.md).\n\n---\n\n## Tiered autonomy (quick reference)\n\n| Tier                   | Actions                                                                        | Stops?                  |\n| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |\n| **Auto**               | read, verify, worktree edits, tests/`tsc`, draft PR body                       | no (logged)             |\n| **Notify-and-proceed** | post Investigation Outcome, open PR **as draft**, post QA-log                  | no (surfaced in digest) |\n| **Require-approval**   | merge, status change, prod/uat PR, RBAC/permission edit, delete, spend         | **yes — always**        |\n| **Escalate**           | spec/scope ambiguity, a scope call, low-confidence gap, `>3–4` files           | **yes — that issue**    |\n\n**Conservative default (until evals earn trust):** treat every\n_Notify-and-proceed_ row as _Require-approval_ — sub-agents prepare and return;\nthe gate commits. The one standing exception is a **reversible** Linear comment\n(Investigation Outcome / QA-log), which the investigator/verifier may post\ndirectly, because the issue _is_ the durable hand-off surface and a comment can be\nedited or deleted. A Linear **status change** is never in that exception.\n\nShip autonomy inward-out: full autonomy on reversible, isolated work (read,\nworktree, tests, drafts); **zero** autonomy on outward, irreversible work until a\nhuman clears each tier. The Auto/Notify tiers only widen as golden + shadow evals\nearn it.\n\n**A human \"continue\" / \"go ahead\" IS the gate approval for the Notify-and-proceed\ntier.** When the person running the workflow says continue, execute the pending\nNotify-and-proceed action (push branch + open PR) **without re-asking** — after\nthe \"dedup again before push/open\" check above. Do **not** re-halt to reconfirm;\nthat reads as stalling. What \"continue\" does **not** unlock: merge, self-approve,\nLinear status change, and any prod/uat or RBAC/permission action — those stay\nRequire-approval and need their own explicit go-ahead each time.\n\nContents of /Users/musta/Code/projects/cds/cds-app-rewrite/.claude/rules/3-workflow/git-branch-and-commit-safety.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):\n\n# Git & Workflow\n\n## Linear-first\n\n- Create a Linear issue **BEFORE** starting a bug fix or feature.\n- Branch naming: `<linear-issue-id>-short-description`\n  (e.g. `CDS-658-fix-migration-column`). **Never** prefix with usernames — strip\n  `<user>/` from Linear-generated names.\n\n## Branch base — always the latest _remote_ ref, never local `main`\n\n- Pick the base by target env: feature/bugfix → `origin/main`; **hotfix →\n  `origin/production`**; env-targeted fix → `origin/qa` / `origin/uat`.\n- **`git fetch origin <base>` first, then branch/worktree off `origin/<base>`.**\n  Local `main` drifts far behind the remote (observed: 210 commits stale), so\n  branching from it — or diffing a feature branch against it — ships/mis-reads a\n  stale base (a stale three-dot diff makes pre-existing errors look PR-introduced).\n- Assert freshness after creating the base: `git rev-parse HEAD` must equal\n  `git rev-parse origin/<base>`. Local `main` is only for the `/start-week`\n  fast-forward; treat it as untrusted otherwise. (The branch-creating agent is\n  `issue-implementer`, Phase 3.)\n\n## Shared working tree — never switch branches silently\n\nMultiple Claude sessions may share this working tree. Switching the checked-out\nbranch (or resetting/stashing) under another session corrupts its work.\n\n- Do NOT `git checkout <branch>` / `git switch` / `git reset --hard` / `git stash`\n  to change working-tree state unless the user explicitly asked in this session.\n- At the start of any git work, run `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and confirm\n  the expected branch. If wrong, STOP and ask — don't silently switch.\n- If a task needs a different branch, prefer an isolated `git worktree` or ask\n  first. Re-verify the branch before editing files.\n\n## Worktree lifecycle — tear down after the PR merges / ticket closes\n\nPer-ticket worktrees accumulate (31 open at once, one run). A worktree is done\nthe moment its **PR is merged or the ticket is closed** — remove it then.\n\n- **Authoritative \"done\" signal is the PR state, not `git branch --merged`.** With\n  squash-merge (this repo's default) a merged branch is **not** an ancestor of\n  `origin/main`, so `--merged` reports it as unmerged. Use\n  `gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged` (or `--state closed`). It survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices or Claude. Claude uses it only for per-viewer conveniences, such as a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section or an unsent draft, and never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers or be read back by Claude.
